method.summary: Each pixel is dry when the gauge is below the level it was dry at in 1984-2021 (JRC water occurrence against the gauge record); the routes of the method run on that water at every level, giving each community the level below which it is at risk or cut off. An anomaly-persistence forecast of the gauge, with the spread of its past errors, turns those levels into probabilities and an expected cut-off date. FIXTURE: the passes are hand-made (fixtures/data/aois/tefe/early_warning_passes.json, invented statuses, no water masks), so the hindcast numbers only exercise the page; they are not results.
limitations: Width is not depth: a channel wide enough on the radar can still be too shallow for a boat.
The water occurrence ends in 2021, and sediment moves channels: the drying map ages.
Lake Tefé does not always follow the gauge on the Solimões: its level lags and differs.
One dry season of radar labels (2026) to check it against.
A hindcast is not a promise: the next drought will not repeat the last one.
